formats.key: mint(address collateralToken, uint256 collateralAmount, uint256 txDeadline, uint256 minFtUSDOut)
effects: Pulls exactly collateralAmount of collateralToken from the signer, using an allowance the signer already gave (_executeMintWithRelayerFee: collateral.safeTransferFrom(payer, address(this), collateralAmount)).

Mints ftUSD at the oracle price (capped by mintPriceHardcapWad), keeps a mint fee in ftUSD, and sends the net ftUSD to the signer. The call reverts if the net is below minFtUSDOut (mintTo: if (ftUSDAmount < minFtUSDOut) revert).
When a circuit breaker is set, the signer's ftUSD can be queued in the breaker instead of arriving at once (_protectedTransferWithTvl: safeTransfer(cb, _amount) and OutflowQueued).
Reverts after txDeadline, unless txDeadline is 0, which means no deadline (_enforceDeadline).
formats.shown: "Buy ftUSD" / "Buy {minFtUSDOut}", with Pay = collateralAmount in collateralToken, Minimum receive = minFtUSDOut in ftUSD, and the Deadline as a date.

findings.title: mint interpolatedIntent shows the minimum as if it were the exact amount bought and leaves out the payment.
findings.evidence: descriptor.json mint: "interpolatedIntent": "Buy {minFtUSDOut}". MintAndRedeem.sol mintTo: the net ftUSD comes from the oracle and only has to be >= minFtUSDOut. The collateral paid (collateralAmount) is missing from the sentence. Case 0 renders "Buy 990000000000 ftUSD".

findings.title: mint Deadline field shows 1970 when txDeadline is 0, but the code reads 0 as no deadline.
findings.evidence: MintAndRedeem.sol _enforceDeadline: if (txDeadline == 0) return. descriptor.json: txDeadline uses format date with encoding timestamp and no note about 0.
findings.fix: Add a label or message that says 0 means no deadline, e.g. "Deadline (0 = none)".

findings.title: mint test case uses an 18-decimal minFtUSDOut for a 6-decimal ftUSD, so it renders 990 billion ftUSD.
findings.evidence: cases/0.json: minFtUSDOut = 0x0dbd2fc137a30000 (0.99e18), screen "Minimum receive": "990000000000 ftUSD". MintAndRedeem.sol header: ftUSD is treated as USD with 6 decimals (FTUSD_SCALE = 1e6).
findings.fix: Set minFtUSDOut to 990000 (0.99 ftUSD) to match 1 USDC paid.

findings.title: mint hardcodes the mainnet ftUSD address for the Sonic (146) deployment as well; not verifiable here.
findings.evidence: descriptor.json: minFtUSDOut params.token = 0xF7D85EC4E7710f71992752eac2111312e73E9C9C, deployments include chainId 146 at 0x0C6f8eC8.... Only the chain 1 constructor args (ftUSD_ = 0xF7D85EC4...) are in the directory.
findings.fix: Confirm that ftUSD has the same address on Sonic. If it does not, split the descriptor per chain or use a per-deployment constant.

findings.title: mint: the circuit breaker can queue the minted ftUSD instead of sending it right away.
findings.evidence: ProtectedContract.sol _protectedTransferWithTvl: if not immediate, IERC20(_token).safeTransfer(cb, _amount) and emit OutflowQueued. _executeMintWithRelayerFee emits MintQueued(recipient, ...).
findings.fix: No descriptor field can show this because it depends on runtime state. A note in the intent or docs could warn about possible delayed delivery.

formats.key: redeem(address collateralToken, uint256 ftUSDAmount, uint256 txDeadline, uint256 minCollateralOut)
effects: Pulls exactly ftUSDAmount of ftUSD from the signer, using an allowance the signer already gave (_executeRedeemWithRelayerFee: safeTransferFrom(p.payer, address(this), p.ftUSDAmount)).
Keeps a redeem fee in ftUSD and burns the rest (core.burn(burnFtUSDAmount)).

Sends collateralToken to the signer through the yield wrapper (wrapper.withdraw(collateralToRecipient, msg.sender)). The amount is priced at the conservative redeem factor and must be >= minCollateralOut, or the call reverts.
The collateral payout can be queued by the wrapper's rate limiter (queueId is returned).
Reverts after txDeadline, unless txDeadline is 0, which means no deadline.
formats.shown: "Sell ftUSD" / "Sell {ftUSDAmount}", with Pay = ftUSDAmount in ftUSD, Minimum receive = minCollateralOut in collateralToken, and the Deadline as a date.

findings.title: redeem interpolatedIntent leaves out what the signer receives in return.
findings.evidence: descriptor.json redeem: "interpolatedIntent": "Sell {ftUSDAmount}". The collateral received (minCollateralOut in collateralToken) only appears as a field. Case 1 renders "Sell 1000000000000 ftUSD".

findings.title: redeem Deadline field shows 1970 when txDeadline is 0, but the code reads 0 as no deadline.
findings.evidence: MintAndRedeem.sol _enforceDeadline: if (txDeadline == 0) return. descriptor.json: txDeadline uses format date with encoding timestamp.
findings.fix: Add a label or message that says 0 means no deadline.

findings.title: redeem test case uses an 18-decimal ftUSDAmount for a 6-decimal ftUSD, so it renders 1 trillion ftUSD for 0.99 USDC.
findings.evidence: cases/1.json: ftUSDAmount = 0x0de0b6b3a7640000 (1e18), screen "Pay": "1000000000000 ftUSD", "Minimum receive": "0.99 USDC". MintAndRedeem.sol: FTUSD_SCALE = 1e6.

findings.title: redeem hardcodes the mainnet ftUSD address for the Sonic (146) deployment as well; not verifiable here.
findings.evidence: descriptor.json: ftUSDAmount params.token = 0xF7D85EC4E7710f71992752eac2111312e73E9C9C, deployments include chainId 146. Only the chain 1 ftUSD_ constructor arg is in the directory.
findings.fix: Confirm that ftUSD has the same address on Sonic, or split the descriptor per chain.

findings.title: redeem: the yield wrapper's rate limiter can queue the collateral payout instead of paying at once.
findings.evidence: MintAndRedeem.sol _executeRedeemWithRelayerFee: queueIdTo = wrapper.withdraw(collateralToRecipient, p.recipient), with the comment "Wrapper is already a ProtectedContract - it handles rate limiting of collateral outflows". redeem returns queueId.
findings.fix: No descriptor field can show this because it depends on runtime state.

couldNotCheck: redeem: the collateral payout to the signer happens inside the per-collateral ftYieldWrapper (wrapper.withdraw(collateralToRecipient, recipient)), whose source is not in the directory. Whether it delivers the full amount, takes a cut or queues it can't be checked.
mint and redeem: the CircuitBreakerV2 contract (attemptOutflow) decides whether the signer's ftUSD is sent at once or queued, and its source is not in the directory.
